title: Platform Observability & SLI Onboarding Playbook
author: Maya Chen
content:
Overview:
This playbook standardizes how platform services are onboarded into Redwood's observability stack, how SLIs/SLOs are defined and registered, and what dashboard/alert templates are required before a service is considered production-ready. It is targeted at platform engineers, service owners, and SREs.

Why this exists:
- Reduce time-to-observable for new services while enforcing consistent SLI definitions.
- Protect product teams from noisy alerts and under-instrumentation.
- Provide a repeatable checklist for production readiness reviews and SLO registration.

Quick summary (one-line):
All platform services must implement the onboarding checklist below, publish SLIs to the SLO library, and deploy a standardized Grafana dashboard and Prometheus alerts prior to enrollment in error-budget policies.

Scope:
- Applies to: services owned by eng-platform, eng-serving-runtime, and core infra teams that expose HTTP/gRPC endpoints, async job processors, or stream processors.
- Exempts: ephemeral experimentation sandboxes and single-run jobs (document exceptions with owner and retention policy).

Ownership and escalation:
- Playbook owner: Platform Observability Guild (contact: platform-observability@redwood.ai)
- Service owner: listed in the service manifest (see onboarding checklist step 1).
- SRE reviewer: assigned during PR review for onboarding (rotation in eng-sre team).

Required artifacts before "production-ready" badge is granted:
1) Service manifest updated in infra repo with contact, component tag, and SLIs.
2) Instrumentation: metrics, structured logs, and traces (see instrumentation section).
3) Grafana dashboard using the platform template (see panels below).
4) Prometheus alert rules committed and linted.
5) SLO registered in SLO library with owner and review cadence.
6) Runbook entry with playbook steps, recovery commands, and rollback guidance.
7) Cost and retention guardrails validated with infra costing tool.

SLI / SLO standardization:
- Default SLI set (apply to HTTP/gRPC services):
  - Availability (success rate): requests with 2xx/3xx over total requests — window=30d, daily burn back.
  - Latency P95: request duration (ms) — window=30d.
  - Latency P99 (for high-priority routes): request duration (ms) — window=7d.
  - Queue depth / backlog for async processors: 99th percentile of queue_length over 1d.
  - Error rate by class: 5xx and client-expected-errors measured separately.

- Default SLO targets (suggested baseline):
  - Availability: 99.95% (soft default for latency-sensitive platform endpoints)
  - Latency P95: <= 200ms for API routes; <= 1s for heavy batch endpoints
  - Latency P99: <= 1s for API routes; <= 5s for batch
  - Queue depth: target mean below 10 items for normal load

- Error budget policy:
  - Burn alerts at 25%, 50%, and 75% of daily error budget consumptions.
  - At 100% consumption trigger immediate on-call page and canary rollback recommendation.

Instrumentation guidelines:
- Metrics: use open-metrics naming conventions. Prefix: redwood_<component>_<metric>. Example: redwood_gateway_request_duration_seconds_bucket
- Labels: service, env, region, route, team, pod (avoid freeform user ids).
- Tracing: include a distributed trace id in logs. Sample at 5% globally; increase to 100% for Canary environments. Use W3C Trace Context.
- Logs: JSON structured logs with level, service, shard, trace_id. Sensitive data must be redacted at the emitter.
- Exporters: Prometheus for metrics, Grafana Tempo for traces, Loki/Datadog native for logs (depending on environment).

Dashboard template (minimum panels):
- Overview row: Success rate (30d), Requests per second (last 1h), Error budget remaining
- Latency row: P50/P95/P99 latency heatmap, latency by route table
- Capacity row: Pod counts, CPU/Memory by pod, OOM rate
- Backpressure row: Queue length, inflight requests, DB pool saturation
- Cost row: estimated GPU/VM-hours consumed (if applicable)

Example table (panel -> query -> suggested thresholds):
| Panel | PromQL example | Alert threshold | Notes |
| Overview: success_rate | (sum(rate(http_requests_total{job=\"%SERVICE%\",code!~\"5..\"}[5m])) / sum(rate(http_requests_total{job=\"%SERVICE%\"}[5m]))) * 100 | < 99.9% for 5m | Service-level availability |
| Latency p95 | histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(http_request_duration_seconds_bucket{job=\"%SERVICE%\"}[5m])) by (le)) | p95 > 0.2 for 10m | Use per-route override |
| Queue depth | max(queue_length{job=\"%SERVICE%\"}) | > 50 for 15m | Backpressure sign |

Prometheus alert rule examples (paste into alerts/prometheus/%SERVICE%.rules.yaml):
---
- alert: ServiceAvailabilityDegraded
  expr: (sum(rate(http_requests_total{job=\"%SERVICE%\",code!~\"5..\"}[5m])) / sum(rate(http_requests_total{job=\"%SERVICE%\"}[5m]))) * 100 < 99.9
  for: 5m
  labels:
    severity: page
    team: %TEAM%
  annotations:
    summary: "%SERVICE% availability below 99.9%"
    runbook: "link_to_runbook/%SERVICE%"

- alert: ServiceLatencyP95High
  expr: histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(http_request_duration_seconds_bucket{job=\"%SERVICE%\"}[5m])) by (le)) > 0.2
  for: 10m
  labels:
    severity: ticket
    team: %TEAM%
  annotations:
    summary: "%SERVICE% p95 latency > 200ms"

Alert categorization and routing:
- severity: page (P0-P1): immediate paging to on-call, include runbook and rollback link.
- severity: ticket (P2): create tracking ticket in PagerDuty/ServiceNow; notify team Slack channel.
- severity: info (P3): create quiet incident in tracking board.

On-call runbook (first-response):
1) Acknowledge the page within 5 minutes.
2) Check the dashboard overview: success rate, requests/s, p95.
3) Determine scope: single route / region / global. Use query: sum(rate(http_requests_total{job=\"%SERVICE%\",route=~\"%ROUTE%\"}[5m])) by (region)
4) If error budget > 25% consumed: begin mitigation. If 100%: escalate to incident.
5) Mitigation steps (in order):
   a) Trigger traffic-shift to canary (kubectl -n %NS% set image deploy/%DEPLOY% %CONTAINER%=%BACKUP_IMAGE%) or toggle edge routing to fallback model.
   b) Scale up pods: kubectl -n %NS% scale deploy/%DEPLOY% --replicas=<replica-count>
   c) Rollback last release: kubectl -n %NS% rollout undo deploy/%DEPLOY% --to-revision=<rev>
   d) If database-related, fail-fast: reduce write traffic via feature-flagging or turn on queueing layer.
6) Record mitigation and update incident ticket with root cause hypotheses.

Post-incident actions and SLO review:
- Run a focused retrospective within 3 business days.
- Update SLO if cadence or traffic patterns change.
- Add synthetic check for failing route if missing.
- If root cause is instrumentation blindspot, update the instrumentation checklist and re-review all services in the component.

Automation and CI gates:
- PRs to production manifests must pass: prometheus-rule-lint, grafana-dashboard-validator, and slo-linter.
- A CI job generates a preview dashboard and a preview PrometheusRule in staging for verification.
- A pre-merge hook rejects alerts with severity:page that lack a runbook link.

Cost and retention guardrails:
- Default metric scrape interval: 15s for infra-critical metrics, 60s for app-level metrics.
- Minimize high-cardinality labels. Use cardinality budget: 100k series per service as starting limit.
- Logs: 30d hot retention, 90d warm depending on service SLAs. Traces: 7d by default; 30d for high-priority customer-facing flows (approve via data governance).

Onboarding checklist (detailed steps):
1) Create service manifest entry in infra/services/ with owner, team, contact, and tags.
2) Implement metrics + export to Prometheus (include example metrics: request_count, request_duration_seconds_bucket, error_count).
3) Add tracing headers and wire into Tempo; verify end-to-end trace in staging.
4) Add Grafana dashboard: use template import ID: 1089 (platform-service-overview). Replace %SERVICE% variables.
5) Add Prometheus rule: commit to alerts/%SERVICE%.rules.yaml and run lint.
6) Register SLO: open a PR against eng-sre/slo-library with SLI queries, SLO target, owner, and review cadence.
7) Create runbook page: copy template and fill recovery steps and CNAs.
8) Schedule a production readiness brief with SRE reviewer and platform guild.
9) After successful verification in staging for 72h under normal load, tag PR with "ready-for-prod" for merge.

Template snippets and helpful links:
- Dashboard template: grafana://dashboard/1089
- SLO library PR template: https://git.internal.redwood.ai/eng-sre/slo-library/templates/slo-pr.md
- Prometheus lint: ./tools/prom-lint --path alerts/%SERVICE%.rules.yaml
- Grafana validator: ./tools/grafana-validate --file dashboards/%SERVICE%.json

Common pitfalls and remediation:
- Missing route labels: leads to noisy aggregate alerts. Remedy: require per-route label in instrumentation.
- High-cardinality metrics from user_id tags: block in code review; suggest using hashed_user_bucket instead.
- Over-aggressive tracing: high cost; use adaptive sampling and increase only for canaries.

Retrospective prompts (post-onboarding, 30d):
- Were the SLO targets appropriate?
- Did dashboards surface the root cause quickly?
- Any alert noise that needs suppression or reclassification?
- Cost impacts of retention and scrape frequency — can we tune?

Change log:
- 2025-08-12: Initial draft (Maya Chen).
- 2025-11-03: Added error budget policy and alert thresholds (Arjun Patel).
- 2026-01-10: Updated dashboard template ID and added CI gate requirements (Lina Gómez).

Appendix: sample CLI checks (copy into runbook):
- Check p95 in last 15m:
  curl -s -G 'https://prometheus.internal/api/v1/query' --data-urlencode 'query=histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(http_request_duration_seconds_bucket{job=\"%SERVICE%\"}[5m])) by (le))' | jq -r '.data.result'
- Verify alert presence:
  kubectl -n monitoring get prometheusrules -o yaml | grep -A3 "%SERVICE%"
- Preview dashboard locally:
  ./tools/grafana-preview dashboards/%SERVICE%.json

End of playbook. For onboarding support, contact platform-observability@redwood.ai or open a PR in infra/services for review.
